core_obligations: Set up the extension (proof lines 10609-10616): the author writes L as the union of its finite subextensions L_i over K and records the Galois-theoretic description of the corresponding subgroups.

One direction (proof lines 10619-10634): assuming the vanishing of H^n(Spec(K), Z/l), the author reduces the general l-power torsion sheaf to sheaves of the form induced from finite quotients, using that an l-power torsion G-module has a finite filtration by such pieces.

The other direction (proof lines 10637-10655): for a finite abelian l-group M with continuous action of the profinite pro-l group, the author produces a G-invariant element controlling the cohomology, which shows that vanishing downstairs forces vanishing upstairs.
proof_roadmap: Write L as the union of its finite subextensions and translate both sides into Galois cohomology.
Reduce an arbitrary l-power torsion sheaf to finite pieces by a filtration.
Use the pro-l nature of the subgroup to transfer vanishing in both directions.
difficulty_reason: The lemma reduces the vanishing of degree-n etale cohomology of Spec(K) with l-power torsion coefficients to the single vanishing H^n_etale(Spec(L), Z/l) for the maximal pro-l extension L of K (statement lines 10598-10607). The proof translates both conditions into Galois cohomology (proof lines 10609-10616), reduces an arbitrary l-power torsion sheaf to finite pieces, and uses the pro-l property of the subgroup to obtain both implications (proof lines 10619-10655). The non-formal content is the reduction of an arbitrary l-power torsion coefficient system to the trivial one. The claim is H2: two reductions, both written out.
